resources.name: 2-1-1 Colorado (United Way of Larimer County)
resources.description: Free, confidential help line that connects you with food, housing, utility help, health care and more anywhere in Larimer County. Call, text your ZIP code to 898-211, or search online.

resources.name: 988 Colorado Mental Health Line
resources.description: Call or text 988 any time for free, confidential support with emotional, mental health or substance use concerns. The old Colorado Crisis Services number (1-844-493-8255) now routes here too.

resources.name: SummitStone Health Partners - Crisis Services
resources.description: Larimer County's community mental health provider. Walk-in crisis care at Longview Acute Care (2260 W Trilby Rd, Fort Collins) is open 24/7. Also offers counseling, substance use treatment and Medicaid-friendly outpatient care.
resources.address: 2260 W Trilby Rd, Fort Collins, CO 80526

resources.name: Crossroads Safehouse
resources.description: 24-hour help for anyone experiencing domestic violence: emergency shelter, safety planning, advocacy and legal help. Confidential and free.

resources.name: Alternatives to Violence
resources.description: Loveland's domestic violence and sexual assault agency. 24-hour crisis line (text 970-669-5157), emergency shelter, advocacy and counseling.

resources.name: Estes Valley Crisis Advocates
resources.description: Support for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault and other crimes in the Estes Valley. After hours, call Estes Park Police dispatch at 970-586-4000 and ask for an advocate.

resources.name: Food Bank for Larimer County - Fort Collins
resources.description: Free groceries through the Fresh Food Share market. Shop like a grocery store, no cost. No paperwork needed for your first visit; bring an ID if you have one.
resources.address: 1301 Blue Spruce Dr, Fort Collins, CO 80524

resources.name: Food Bank for Larimer County - Loveland
resources.description: Free groceries through the Fresh Food Share market in Loveland. Also the pickup point for senior food boxes (CSFP) for adults 60+.

resources.name: Vindeket Foods
resources.description: Pay-what-you-can grocery market that rescues surplus food. Everyone is welcome; pay nothing if you need to. No questions asked.

resources.name: FoCo Cafe
resources.description: Pay-what-you-can restaurant serving a healthy lunch to everyone. Pay what you can afford, volunteer an hour for a meal, or eat free.

resources.name: Food Not Bombs - Fort Collins
resources.description: Volunteer group that shares free meals and groceries. No paperwork, no questions. They serve with Clothe the People. The Oak Street Mennonite Fellowship building they used is closed, so the spot can move. Check Instagram before you go.
resources.hours: Often Wed 5-7pm and Sunday afternoon; some Thu/Sat park shares. Confirm this week's location on Instagram.

resources.name: UCHealth Family Medicine Center Food Pantry
resources.description: Free food pantry open to anyone in the community, located inside the Family Medicine Center. Ask at the front desk for Suite 109.
resources.address: 1025 Pennock Pl, Suite 109, Fort Collins, CO 80524

resources.name: Salvation Army - Fort Collins
resources.description: Food pantry, free breakfast (Mon, Wed, Thu 8:30-9:30am), clothing help and seasonal assistance. Call ahead for pantry hours.
resources.address: 3901 S Mason St, Fort Collins, CO 80525

resources.name: St. John's Lutheran Church Food Pantry
resources.description: Weekly food pantry and clothing closet open to anyone in need. No proof of income required.
resources.address: 305 E Elizabeth St, Fort Collins, CO 80524

resources.name: Mobile Food Pantry at Foothills Unitarian Church
resources.description: Food Bank for Larimer County mobile pantry with free fresh produce and groceries. Drive-through or walk up.

resources.name: NoCo CommUNITY Store
resources.description: Free community pantry and clothing closet run by volunteers. Take what you need; no paperwork.
resources.address: 120 W Saturn Dr, Unit A, Fort Collins, CO 80525
resources.hours: Call 2-1-1 or check their social pages for current hours

resources.name: House of Neighborly Service - Loveland
resources.description: Food pantry, clothing, hygiene items, and help with rent, utilities and prescriptions for people in the Loveland area.

resources.name: House of Neighborly Service - Berthoud
resources.description: Food pantry and emergency assistance (rent, utilities, clothing) for Berthoud-area residents.

resources.name: Loveland's Community Kitchen
resources.description: Free hot dinner every day of the week for anyone who is hungry. No questions asked.

resources.name: Salvation Army - Loveland
resources.description: Food pantry, emergency assistance and seasonal help for the Loveland and Berthoud area.
resources.address: 840 N Lincoln Ave, Suite 101, Loveland, CO 80537

resources.name: ServSafe Food Handler
resources.description: The kitchen card restaurants actually know. About 90 minutes online, $15, English or Spanish. Valid 3 years. Helps you get hired or a raise at fast food, grocery, and cafe jobs. Ask the Larimer Workforce Center if they can cover the fee.

resources.name: OSHA 10-Hour card (construction or general industry)
resources.description: The safety card warehouses, construction, and manufacturing often want. Use OSHA's official trainer list only — fake 'OSHA certified' sites will not give you a real card. The course is not free; ask WIOA at the Workforce Center to pay. A forklift 'certificate' sold online is not OSHA training; your employer has to train you on the lift.

resources.name: Workforce Center paid job training (WIOA)
resources.description: If you are homeless, in recovery, on SNAP or TANF, or otherwise struggling to work, Larimer's Career Transition team can often pay for a real certificate: food handler or ServSafe Manager, OSHA-10, CNA, CDL, and similar. This is the same Workforce Center as the Jobs card — ask specifically for training money, not just resume help.
resources.address: 200 W Oak St, Suite 5000, Fort Collins, CO 80521

resources.name: CareerReady Colorado Certificate (WorkKeys)
resources.description: A skills certificate signed by the governor: applied math, workplace documents, and graphic literacy. Many employers treat it as proof you can handle a first job even without a long work history. Ask the Workforce Center (970-498-6600) to schedule it — do not pay a random website for a fake NCRC.
resources.address: 200 W Oak St, Suite 5000, Fort Collins, CO 80521
resources.hours: By appointment at a workforce center

resources.name: Colorado Shines PDIS (child-care credentials)
resources.description: Free state courses and an Early Childhood Professional Credential. Daycares and preschools hire people who have the required health-and-safety hours. Pair it with Colorado Mandatory Reporter training. Create an account through Colorado Shines, then take PDIS courses.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (Colorado classes)
resources.description: One-day certificate in spotting a mental-health or substance-use crisis and getting someone help. SummitStone often runs it free in Fort Collins. Useful for peer work, shelters, restaurants, and any job that deals with people in crisis. Search the Colorado class calendar — do not pay a random online knockoff.
resources.hours: Scheduled day-long classes; some are free

resources.name: Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS)
resources.description: State peer-recovery credential for people with lived experience of addiction or mental illness who want to get paid to walk with others. You need about 60 training hours, supervised peer hours, and usually two years in your own recovery. Application and exam run about $295; ask COPA about scholarships and ask SummitStone or the Health District about peer jobs.

resources.name: Colorado QMAP (medication administration)
resources.description: State qualification to give meds in assisted living, group homes, and some disability programs. Start with the free CDPHE prep course on CO.TRAIN, then take an approved class (often $90–$120 locally). Must be 18. Group homes and Foothills Gateway-type jobs ask for this.

resources.name: McDonald's Archways to Opportunity
resources.description: If you already work at a participating McDonald's: free high-school diploma, English classes, and college tuition help. Crew usually need 90 days and about 15 hours a week. Ask your GM — this is how a fast-food job turns into a raise or a diploma, not a public food-handler class.

resources.name: NWCG S-190 Introduction to Wildland Fire Behavior
resources.description: Free federal intro course used for seasonal wildland-fire and conservation-crew jobs. Take it on the Wildland Fire Learning Portal. An official firefighter card still needs S-130 plus a fire department or crew — this class alone is the usual first step, not a job offer.
